observed_result.held_out: down high is never generated correctly by either group at the default 80 epochs (at 320 epochs the core gets it in two of three seeds).
observed_result.reading: Frames, audio and timeline are complete for every clip, and temporal change, sync and packager failure are each measured and tested. At the default 80 epochs the model is weak: the core gets 3 or 4 of 5 seen clips right and 0 to 3 of them in sync; most sync errors are -1 because the dot's path is not sharp enough for the judge to find the edge arrival, while the core places the beep on the target frame 7 in 16 of 18 clips against 0 of 18 for the frozen-core control and reaches a lower MSE. Longer training changes the picture (post-hoc observations, not the recorded default): at 160 epochs the frozen-core control is ahead, and at 320 epochs the core gets 4 or 5 of 5 seen clips in sync against 0 to 3 for the control, with the held-out clip right in two seeds.

longer_training.160: seed 1: core seen 4/5 held-out 1/1 in sync 3/5, frozen core seen 5/5 in sync 4/5; seed 2: core seen 4/5 held-out 1/1 in sync 3/5, frozen core seen 5/5 in sync 4/5; seed 3: core seen 3/5 held-out 0/1 in sync 1/5, frozen core seen 4/5 in sync 3/5
longer_training.320: seed 1: core seen 5/5 held-out 1/1 in sync 5/5, frozen core seen 4/5 in sync 2/5; seed 2: core seen 4/5 held-out 1/1 in sync 4/5, frozen core seen 4/5 in sync 0/5; seed 3: core seen 5/5 held-out 0/1 in sync 5/5, frozen core seen 4/5 in sync 3/5

observed_result.reproducibility: The rerun at the same commit produced byte-identical video.json, summary.txt and native clip files; packaged containers differ only by ffmpeg's run-specific metadata.

assumption_statement: The fixture is a single dot and one beep; it proves the frame, audio and timeline pipeline and its synchronisation measure, not open-ended video generation. The decoder is a fixed clamp; the prompt reaches the frames and the audio only through the core. Pixel or sample MSE says nothing about perceptual quality. The frozen-core control trains only the encoder and readout.
limitations: One dot and one beep on 8x8 frames; no claim about natural video, resolution or perceptual quality.
The held-out condition is never generated correctly at the default budget.

At the default budget sync is weak (0 to 3 of 5 seen clips in sync). The core-versus-frozen comparison changes with the training budget (the control is ahead at 160 epochs, the core at 320), so no stable conclusion about the core's own contribution is drawn; the longer runs are post-hoc observations, not a chosen default.
Packaged containers are not byte-reproducible because ffmpeg stamps run-specific metadata; the native files are.
Real authorised video data is TSK-11 and remains blocked_data.
